Jupiter is so massive that it is more than twice the combined mass of all the other planets in the Solar System.
Venus rotates so slowly, and in the opposite direction to most planets, that its day is longer than its year.
Saturn's average density is lower than water — it would theoretically float in a large enough ocean.
Neptune has the fastest recorded winds in the Solar System, exceeding 2,000 km/h.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to travel from the Sun to Earth.
A solar day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) lasts about 176 Earth days due to its slow spin and eccentric orbit.
Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is larger in diameter than the planet Mercury.
Titan, Saturn's largest moon, has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane and ethane on its surface.
Mars is home to Olympus Mons, the tallest known volcano in the Solar System, roughly three times the height of Mount Everest.
Uranus rotates almost completely on its side, likely the result of an ancient massive collision.
The Sun accounts for about 99.8% of the total mass of the entire Solar System.
One million Earths could fit inside the volume of the Sun.
Earth's magnetic field is generated by the churning motion of molten iron in its outer core.
The Great Red Spot on Jupiter is a storm larger than Earth that has persisted for at least 150 years.
Pluto was reclassified from a planet to a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union in 2006.
Europa, a moon of Jupiter, is thought to hide a deep subsurface ocean beneath its icy crust.
Enceladus, a small moon of Saturn, sprays plumes of water-ice from its south pole into space.
The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy roughly 100,000 light-years across.
Our Solar System sits in the Orion Arm, a minor spiral arm about 26,000–27,000 light-years from the galactic center.
Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at our galaxy's center, has a mass of roughly 4 million Suns.
Venus's surface pressure is about 92 times that of Earth — similar to being nearly a kilometer underwater.
Mercury has water ice hidden in permanently shadowed craters near its poles, despite its extreme daytime heat.
Neptune was discovered in 1846 through mathematical prediction before anyone directly observed it through a telescope.
The rings of Saturn are made almost entirely of ice and rock particles ranging from dust grains to house-sized chunks.
Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is the most distant human-made object and has entered interstellar space.
A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years — it has completed only one orbit since its discovery in 1846.
The four Galilean moons of Jupiter — Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto — were first observed by Galileo Galilei in 1610.
Mars's atmosphere is less than 1% as dense as Earth's, made almost entirely of carbon dioxide.
Light from the center of the Milky Way takes about 26,000 years to reach Earth.
Io, a moon of Jupiter, is the most volcanically active body known in the Solar System.
The largest known canyon system in the Solar System, Valles Marineris on Mars, stretches roughly the width of the continental United States.
Saturn's moon Titan is the only moon in the Solar System known to have a dense atmosphere.
Comparing surface gravity, a person weighing 70 kg on Earth would weigh only about 11.9 kg-equivalent on the Moon.
The observable universe is estimated to be about 93 billion light-years in diameter.
Black holes like Sagittarius A* do not 'suck in' everything nearby — objects can safely orbit them at a distance, just as planets orbit stars.
